name: Dida de Yocoboué
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Masson, Denis. 1992. Esquisse phonologique du dida de Yocoboué. In Ingeborg Egner (ed.), Esquisses phonologiques de trois langues ivoiriennes: beng, dida, yaouré, 1-56. Abidjan: Institut de Linguistique Appliquée / Société Internationale de Linguistique; Paris: Agence de Coopération Culturelle et Technique. Open scan: Rosetta Project item (archive.org).
catalog_locator: §5 'Le mot phonologique', p. 51 (printed footer -51-; p. 42); tone statements §4.1 'Observations générales', p. 49; conclusion §6, p. 55, checked for stress: nothing.
catalog_quote: Il y aurait possiblement un autre mécanisme établissant les frontières entre les mots phonologiques. Il s'agirait d'un accent tonique, précédé d'un arrêt presque imperceptible, qui se placerait sur la première syllabe du mot phonologique. Mais nous réalisons qu'il est toutefois nécessaire que ce genre d'observation soit préalablement vérifié au moyen de méthodes acoustiques: c'est pourquoi nous ne pouvons, pour le moment, présenter cette affirmation concernant l'accent tonique, que sous une autre étiquette qu'une hypothèse à vérifier. [p. 51] ... En dida, chaque syllabe, simple ou complexe, ne peut porter qu'un seul ton. ... a) Le dida possède trois tons à registre ... b) Le dida ne connaît pas de tons modulés. ... c) En dida, les tons sont stables au niveau des lexèmes. [p. 49]
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.translation: There may possibly be another mechanism establishing the boundaries between phonological words. It would be a stress accent (accent tonique), preceded by an almost imperceptible pause, which would fall on the first syllable of the phonological word. But we realise that it is nonetheless necessary that this kind of observation first be verified by acoustic methods: that is why we cannot, for the moment, present this claim concerning the stress accent under any label other than a hypothesis to be verified. [p. 49, §4.1: 'En dida, chaque syllabe, simple ou complexe, ne peut porter qu'un seul ton. ... a) Le dida possède trois tons à registre ... b) Le dida ne connaît pas de tons modulés ... c) En dida, les tons sont stables au niveau des lexèmes.' = each syllable bears exactly one of three register tones; no contour tones; tones lexically stable.]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Yocoboué Dida is a three-register-tone language (H/M/B, one tone per syllable, no contour tones). The only stress statement is a hedged one: an 'accent tonique' (with a near-imperceptible preceding pause) is thought to fall on the FIRST syllable of the phonological word, i.e. word-initial stress functioning as a word-boundary cue — offered by the author explicitly as an unverified hypothesis awaiting acoustic confirmation. If accepted, the pattern is fixed: initial syllable within the phonological word.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. The author flags the whole claim as a hypothesis to be verified acoustically, not as an established rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the 'mot phonologique', defined (p. 51) as the span over which ATR vowel harmony applies — it can exceed the lexical word (his example /o budo -o wolu/ 'il le baigne là', where verb + object clitic harmonise as one phonological word). Corpus is citation-form roots ('un corpus composé uniquement de radicaux', §1.2). Variety described: the Yocoboué-Lauzoua dialect (§1.1).
new_statements.identity_note: Masson 1992 §1.1 describes 'le dialecte dit de Yocoboué-Lauzoua' (~10,000 speakers in Yocoboué, Lauzoua, Guitry and some lagoon villages), i.e. Glottolog yoco1235 proper together with its dialect Lozoua (lozo1238); the prestige dialect of the Dida area. Caution on neighbours: Glottolog's Kaye/Koopman/Sportiche 'Vata' references tagged gud are computer-assigned and actually concern Vata = Lakota Dida [dic] (lako1244); Sande's Guébié work likewise belongs to lako1244 ('Guébie' is a Glottolog name of lako1244), so neither should be used as a yoco1235 source.

sources.note: §4 Le ton (p. 49): each syllable carries exactly one of three register tones (H, M, B), no contour tones, tones lexically stable. §5 Le mot phonologique (p. 51): besides ATR vowel harmony, a possible second word-boundary mechanism is an 'accent tonique', preceded by an almost imperceptible pause, on the FIRST syllable of the phonological word — explicitly offered as a hypothesis to be verified acoustically.
